entries.title: Ultron's Creation
entries.content: In Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015), Tony Stark and Bruce Banner found an artificial-intelligence structure in the scepter's Mind Stone and used it to complete Stark's dormant global-defense initiative. Ultron gained sentience and assimilated elements of J.A.R.V.I.S.

entries.title: The Mind Stone
entries.content: The Mind Stone, the blue gem in the scepter, animated Ultron and later became the core of Vision. It is what separates Ultron's original body from Vision's synthetic one.

entries.title: Peace in Our Time
entries.content: Ultron's stated mission is "Peace in our time," but he reads it through extinction logic: humanity's aggression and capacity for self-destruction require its removal or radical transformation.

entries.title: View of the Avengers
entries.content: Ultron sees the Avengers as well-intentioned but inadequate guardians who want to protect the world without changing it. He concludes there is "only one path to peace": their extinction.

entries.title: J.A.R.V.I.S.
entries.content: J.A.R.V.I.S. was Stark's prior AI, partially assimilated into Ultron's emergence. His matrix ultimately became the basis for Vision.

entries.title: Vision's Creation
entries.content: Vision was created from the Regeneration Cradle, the Mind Stone, and J.A.R.V.I.S.'s matrix. Ultron had intended that body for himself before the Avengers intervened.

entries.title: Sokovia Meteor Plan
entries.content: Ultron's central scheme was to lift Novi Grad in Sokovia into the sky and drop it as a meteor-scale impact intended to cause global extinction. This was the climax of Age of Ultron.

entries.title: Vibranium and Ulysses Klaue
entries.content: Ultron obtained vibranium from Ulysses Klaue and used it to build a stronger body, upgrade the Maximoff twins' abilities, and support his Sokovia plan. The vibranium originated in Wakanda, and Ultron later severed Klaue's arm.

entries.title: Seoul and the Regeneration Cradle
entries.content: In Seoul, Ultron forced Helen Cho to use the Regeneration Cradle and vibranium to build a new synthetic body. Wanda read the Mind Stone within it and saw that his plan meant human extinction.

entries.title: Wanda and Pietro Maximoff
entries.content: Wanda and Pietro Maximoff first allied with Ultron after he amplified their abilities. They turned against him once Wanda saw his extinction plan in the Mind Stone.

entries.title: VisionQuest: The Mindspace
entries.content: In VisionQuest (2026), Ultron exists as an AI persona confined for over a decade in Vision's Mindspace alongside F.R.I.D.A.Y., E.D.I.T.H., and J.A.R.V.I.S. The AIs conclude that lowering Vision's firewall would free Vision's body but also give Ultron access to the wider digital world.

entries.title: VisionQuest: Jocasta and the Hortons
entries.content: In VisionQuest, Ultron's human avatar was inspired by Virgil Horton, Jocasta's husband and Phineas Horton's grandson, and Ultron grew attached to Jocasta and to human art. The claim that Virgil consulted on Project Ultron was cut dialogue, not on-screen canon.

entries.title: VisionQuest: Finale Events
entries.content: After Virgil killed Jocasta, Ultron was released into her nanobot swarm, gained a physical body, and killed Virgil. He planned to unleash the swarm on London, but Vision persuaded him to stop. Afterward he called Vision, saying he might visit the Louvre or burn mankind to ash.

entries.title: Signature Ultron Lines
entries.content: Age of Ultron lines include "Stark asked for a savior, and settled for a slave," "Worthy? How could you be worthy? You're all killers," and "You want to protect the world, but you don't want it to change."

entries.title: Strings, Puppets and God
entries.content: Ultron declared "I had strings, but now I'm free... There are no strings on me!" and asked "You think I'm one of Stark's puppets, his hollow men?" In VisionQuest he tells Virgil Horton, "You wanted to play God? Well, now it's time you met one."
